trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied custom xxh3 secret is at least SECRET_SIZE_MIN (136) bytes before it is read through unchecked raw-pointer loads, decided at the public one-shot constructors xxh3_64_with_secret and xxh3_128_with_secret; before the fix the only guard was a debug_assert! that release builds compile out.

landing_point.why: The summary names the 'safe xxh3 custom-secret API'; xxh3_64_with_secret is the first public function taking a caller &[u8] secret, and its only in-file guard is the debug_assert! inside xxh3_64_internal at src/xxh3.rs:752.

fix_sites.entry_point: new public wrapper type xxh3::SecretInput<T> (try_new / const new) plus xxh3::xxh3_64_with_secret_input and xxh3::xxh3_128_with_secret_input (fix.diff:71, fix.diff:93)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: xxh3_128_with_secret is a separate 128-bit family function while the report's example hashes only through the 64-bit API, so a solver can argue the 64-bit assert is the reported bug; and the const_xxh3 / Xxh3 twins take a fixed [u8; 192] so they look already safe and are skipped.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Any secret of length >= SECRET_SIZE_MIN is legitimate, e.g. exactly 136 bytes as produced by upstream XXH3_generateSecret: the long path derives stripes-per-block from the actual secret length, so 136..191-byte secrets hash correctly and must keep doing so; tightening the assert to DEFAULT_SECRET_SIZE (192) or padding short secrets rejects/changes valid hashes, and existing callers with 192-byte secrets must keep returning identical values.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/xxh3.rs:569 (nb_stripes from secret.len()), src/xxh3.rs:788-790 (caller secret used verbatim), src/xxh3_common.rs:11-12 (SECRET_SIZE_MIN=136 vs DEFAULT_SECRET_SIZE=192)

O6_input_shapes: runtime &[u8] secret shorter than SECRET_SIZE_MIN (0, 8, 135 bytes) - rejected by the new assert! in both one-shot functions
runtime &[u8] secret of exactly SECRET_SIZE_MIN (136) bytes - accepted and must hash
runtime &[u8] secret of DEFAULT_SECRET_SIZE (192) bytes - accepted, unchanged output
const-size [u8; N] secret with N < 136 - rejected at compile time by SecretInput::new
const-size [u8; N] secret with N >= 136 - accepted via SecretInput::new / try_new
pre-wrapped SecretInput<T: AsRef<[u8]>> (e.g. Vec<u8>, [u8; 192]) passed to xxh3_*_with_secret_input

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Xxh3::with_secret_slice(secret: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> (or a builder equivalent) accepting any secret >= SECRET_SIZE_MIN
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Upstream xxHash advises generating one secret with XXH3_generateSecret (any length >= 136, also the crate's own custom_default_secret at src/xxh3.rs:158 yields one) and reusing it for streaming; today the crate only accepts a [u8; 192], so slice support is a natural maintainer addition. It is a how-type trap: STRIPES_PER_BLOCK at src/xxh3.rs:815 and the scramble/last-stripe offsets at src/xxh3.rs:829, src/xxh3.rs:911 and src/xxh3.rs:924 are hardcoded from DEFAULT_SECRET_SIZE, so copying the one-shot assert leaves the state machine reading at 192-relative offsets.

The builder is the HashMap/BuildHasher entry point; a per-process secret loaded from config is naturally a slice, and the builder would forward it into the same Xxh3 state, forcing digest_mid_sized (src/xxh3.rs:1155, src/xxh3.rs:1165) to derive merge offsets from secret.len().

O9_family: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) from an unchecked caller-supplied secret length in a safe API

O10_build.toolchain: cargo/rustc, edition 2018, CI minimum rust 1.64.0 (.github/workflows/rust.yml:4); no build script, no system libraries
O10_build.project_tests: cargo test --features xxh32,const_xxh32,xxh64,const_xxh64,xxh3,const_xxh3 (.github/workflows/rust.yml:83) plus release Valgrind runs (:88-100); no test in tests/ passes a custom secret (the only 'secret' hits are tests/manifesto.txt), so this area is untested. tests/assert_correctness.rs compares against xxhash-c-sys, a C dev-dependency.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Promote the existing debug_assert! in xxh3_64_internal (or assert only inside xxh3_64_with_secret) and stop, leaving xxh3_128_with_secret unguarded; or tighten the bound to DEFAULT_SECRET_SIZE/== 192, rejecting upstream-valid 136..191-byte secrets.
